title: Quantum Belief Characterization: A Multi-Shot Notion of Equivalence
authors: Mingxuan Liu, Pavel Sekatski, Valerio Scarani
abstract: A recent formulation of quantum belief showed that quantum retrodiction depends not only on the reduced density operator of the system of interest, but also on correlations with a hidden reference system, which leads to the notion of quantum belief equivalence. In this paper we formulate a multi-shot problem, where the extended posterior obtained after one update is used again as the prior for the next update. We first define a formal notion of $n$-shot equivalence and derive several propositions for arbitrary extended beliefs. We then argue that the agent must also specify why the data obtained in different rounds concern the same underlying object. Through the quantum de Finetti representation, this narrows the one-copy belief to a special class: candidate-state ensemble belief. In that sector, we show that two beliefs are $n$-shot equivalent if and only if their $(n+1)$-th moments are equal. We also give a physical interpretation of this moment condition and illustrate it through the equivalence between Haar priors and projective-design priors at bounded update depth.
summary: This paper formalizes 'multi-shot equivalence' for quantum beliefs, which governs how beliefs should behave after multiple sequential updates. It establishes that for a specific class of beliefs, this multi-shot equivalence is mathematically equivalent to matching the $(n+1)$-th moments. This provides a powerful, quantifiable diagnostic tool for assessing the consistency of iterative quantum inference.
main_problem: The paper develops a formal, multi-shot notion of equivalence for quantum beliefs, extending the single-shot concept by analyzing iterative updates.
main_result: For candidate-state ensemble beliefs, multi-shot equivalence is shown to be equivalent to the equality of the $(n+1)$-th moments of the underlying belief structures.
method: The analysis employs the quantum de Finetti representation and analyzes the consistency of iterative updates using moment matching and functional analysis techniques.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum beliefs, represented by extended density operators on a system of interest ($S$) and a hidden reference system ($R$). The process models sequential, multi-shot updates based on quantum measurements.
key_observables: The final posterior marginal on the system $S$ after $n$ updates, and the $(n+1)$-th moments of the belief structure.
important_parameters: The number of shots, $n$, and the structure of the admissible update channels $(E, \sigma)$.
main_assumptions: The physical interpretation of iterative updating requires assuming a source model (conditionally i.i.d. source) to simplify the equivalence condition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining single-shot quantum belief equivalence to formulating the multi-shot update process. It then uses the quantum de Finetti representation to restrict the problem to candidate-state ensembles, culminating in the moment-matching criterion for equivalence.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous mathematical framework for characterizing belief consistency across multiple measurements is relevant to quantum process tomography and sequential quantum estimation protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Multi-shot equivalence of quantum beliefs. Starting from two extended beliefs β and γ on SR, the same admissible update sequence is applied. The beliefs are n-shot equivalent, β ∼n γ, when the final posterior marginals on S agree for any such sequence of length n.

Figure 1 illustrates this definition: the relation β ∼n γ holds when applying the same admissible update sequence to the two extended beliefs always yields the same final posterior marginal on system S. The notion is strictly stronger than single-shot equivalence because it requires the equality of the marginals of final belief after arbitrary sequences of updates rather than after only one.
